nodes.label: Novelty Statement for V = 4ν/3
nodes.rationale: Closed as unresolved, and deliberately so: a paper that names its own unchecked prior art is in a stronger position than one that claims priority and is corrected. The four named documents are a finite, specified task whose completion either confirms the result or improves the historical record.

nodes.label: V = 4ν/3 (bracket-width over interpolation-error ratio)
nodes.rationale: Assessed ~75 % novel. The structural argument for the higher end is that the quantity has no use in a fitting paradigm — one computes bracket-width-over-interpolation-error only when constructing brackets, and the literature is uniformly predictive, so absence is a reason rather than a failure to find.

nodes.label: Four Unchecked Prior-Art Documents (Edlén, Ritz PZ, Paschen & Götze, Dunz)
Ritz 1908 (Astrophysical Journal version, read in full)
nodes.rationale: Contains the series formula, the combination principle and the magnetic-atom model but no error bound of any kind. It does hold the qualitative ancestor: differences and sums of observed wave-numbers are more accurate than working through fitted constants — the principle the bracket formalises, unquantified.

nodes.label: E(X) as a Closure Defect, Not Claimed Novel
nodes.rationale: Closure operators, Galois connections and formal-concept analysis are established mathematics; what is offered is the application — computing the closure defect of an index, and finding the periodic table's is 36 while Λ's is 0.
